companies.name: adidas AG
notes: IFRS in every year 2007-2025, EUR, fiscal year ending 31 December. All 19 years FY2007-FY2025 were found in adidas's own annual reports; no year or field is missing.

Scope break (Reebok): FY2007-FY2019 are consolidated totals including the Reebok business. From Q1 2021 Reebok was reclassified to discontinued operations and the sale closed on 1 March 2022, so FY2020 and FY2021 revenue, operating profit and total assets are the continuing-operations figures (ex-Reebok) used in adidas's later ten-year overviews. FY2020 is therefore shown as revenue 18,435 / operating profit 746 (continuing) instead of the 19,844 / 751 first published in the 2020 annual report, and is flagged restated; its net income attributable (432, EPS 2.21) is the 2020 annual report figure including a +13m gain from discontinued operations (prior-year divestments), and balance-sheet items are as reported (Reebok was not yet held for sale at 31 December 2020). Part of the apparent 2019-to-2020 revenue drop (23,640 -> 18,435) is this scope change, not a like-for-like decline.

FY2016 revenue and operating profit (18,483 / 1,582) are the continuing-operations figures restated in the 2018 and 2025 ten-year overviews after the 2017 divestiture of TaylorMade, Adams Golf, Ashworth and CCM Hockey; the 2016 annual report itself showed 19,291 / 1,491. FY2011 is the IAS 8 restatement published in the 2012 report (revenue 13,322 vs 13,344; net income attributable 613 vs 671). FY2017 balance-sheet figures are the IAS 8 restatement of the 2018 report.

netIncome is net income attributable to shareholders, i.e. including discontinued operations: FY2021 includes a EUR 666m gain from the Reebok discontinued operation and FY2022 a EUR 384m gain, so those two years are not comparable with the continuing-operations figures shown in adidas's own overviews (2021: 1,492; 2022: 254).

dilutedEPS is the diluted EPS from continuing and discontinued operations so that it ties to netIncome (e.g. 2025: 7.51, 2022: 3.34, 2021: 10.90). adidas's ten-year overviews instead print EPS and net income excluding the goodwill impairments of FY2012-FY2015 (265 / 52 / 78 / 34 million) and the FY2017 one-off tax charge of EUR 76m, which is why the overview rows differ from the reported statements used here (e.g. FY2015 overview: net income 668 and EPS 3.54 vs reported 634 and 3.15; FY2017 overview: 1,173 and 7.00 vs reported 1,097 and 5.38).

operatingIncome is the reported operating profit of the consolidated income statement, i.e. after the goodwill impairment losses charged in FY2009-FY2015 where applicable (FY2012: 920 after 265; FY2013: 1,181 after 52; FY2014: 883 after 78; FY2015: 1,059 after 34).

totalDebt is the sum of the published balance-sheet lines short-term borrowings + long-term borrowings + current and non-current lease liabilities (identical to the 'composition of adjusted net borrowings' note less pensions and factoring). IFRS 16 was applied from 1 January 2019 without restating 2018, so totalDebt jumps from 1,675 (2018) to 4,770 (2019) purely because leases came on balance sheet; pre-2019 operating leases were off balance sheet. Lease-free gross borrowings for 2025 are EUR 2,642m (2024: 2,485m).

capex is purchases of property, plant and equipment only, stored negative; adidas reports purchases of intangible assets separately (2025: 114, 2024: 121, 2023: 141, 2022: 191, 2021: 173, 2020: 64, 2019: 110, 2018: 96, 2017: 74, 2016: 65, 2015: 49, 2014: 49, 2013: 52, 2012: 58, 2011: 58, 2010: 42, 2009: 46, 2008: 60, 2007: 55 million). Yahoo Finance's capex figure adds intangibles, which is why Yahoo's 2025 capex (about EUR 478m) differs from the 363m reported here.

operatingCashFlow is the consolidated total including discontinued operations as presented in the cash flow statement (2021: 3,192m = 2,873m + 320m; 2020: 1,486m = 1,489m - 3m). FY2023 and FY2022 are the figures adjusted for IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting as published in the following year's report, hence restated = true: FY2023 2,550m in the 2024 annual report (the 2023 annual report showed 2,630m), FY2022 -479m in the 2023 annual report (=-394m continuing -85m discontinued; the 2022 annual report itself showed -543m = -458m - 85m).

dividendPerShare is the dividend for the reporting year as printed in adidas's ten-year overview. FY2019 is nil: the EUR 3.85 proposed for 2019 was withdrawn when the COVID-19 syndicated loan suspended dividend payments and no dividend was paid in 2020. FY2025 (EUR 2.80) was still subject to AGM approval when the 2025 annual report was published.

sharesOutstanding is the number of shares outstanding at year-end (in thousands in the source, converted to units). FY2019 employees 65,194 is the restated count including temporary contracts of up to six months (originally 59,333).

Cross-check against Yahoo Finance (docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json) for the last four years: the snapshot converts the P&L and cash flow at average month-end rates and the balance sheet at the closing rate, so each USD figure has to be divided by the rate that fits its year. Taking the rate implied by Yahoo's own gross profit (2025: 1.1324, 2024: 1.0802, 2023: 1.0847, 2022: 1.0517), revenue comes out at 24,810 / 23,686 / 21,428 / 22,511m EUR against 24,811 / 23,683 / 21,427 / 22,511m reported and net income at 1,340 / 764 / -75 / 612m against 1,340 / 764 / -75 / 612m reported - every line within 0.1%. Yahoo's operatingIncome is also within 0.3% (2025: 2,061 vs 2,056). Two confirmations of the figures used here: Yahoo's operating cash flow converts to -479m for FY2022 and 2,550m for FY2023, i.e. the hyperinflation-adjusted values, and its capex converts to 477 / 540 / 504 / 695m, exactly purchases of PP&E plus intangibles in those years. Balance-sheet items convert at the closing rate and match too (2025: total assets 20,262, equity 5,776, total debt 5,555 vs 5,554 reported), except cash: Yahoo shows 1,520m for FY2025 against adidas's 1,617m and 1,812m for FY2022 against 798m reported, so its cash line is a different definition.

companies.name: Adyen N.V.
gaps: FY2007-FY2013 (all fields): nothing published. Adyen was founded in 2006 and listed on Euronext Amsterdam in June 2018; the earliest consolidated financial statements it has published are the audited FY2015 statements, which carry FY2014 comparatives (June 2018 IPO prospectus). No annual report, results release or prospectus covering FY2007-FY2013 was found on the IR site.
FY2014 dilutedEPS: earnings per share is not presented in the FY2015 statements and the prospectus has no earlier EPS disclosure.
FY2015 dilutedEPS: not presented. The FY2015 and FY2016 statements in the prospectus contain no EPS note (the FY2017 statements, the first with an EPS note, show only FY2017 and FY2016).
FY2016 dilutedEPS: not presented in the FY2016 statements and no later opened document restates an FY2016 EPS.
FY2014 sharesOutstanding: the prospectus' historic share capital table starts at FY2015 (29,368,082 issued shares); no FY2014 share count is published.
FY2014 employees: no FTE figure is published for 2014; the prospectus' FTE-at-year-end table covers 2015-2017 only.
notes: All figures are IFRS as adopted by the EU, the only basis Adyen has ever reported on (its first published statements are the FY2015 statements with FY2014 comparatives). Amounts were read in EUR thousands and scaled to units; EUR is the reporting currency in every year.

revenue is the top line of the consolidated statement of comprehensive income as Adyen labels it: 'Revenue' for FY2014-FY2023 and 'Non-interest revenue' for FY2024-FY2025 (the same line renamed in AR2024). This is the gross measure that includes interchange and scheme fees that Adyen pays to issuers and networks and charges on to merchants. It is therefore NOT a like-for-like series across FY2023: Adyen stopped grossing up interchange from FY2023, so revenue falls from EUR 8,935,611k (FY2022) to EUR 1,863,406k (FY2023) on a change of presentation, not of business. Costs incurred from financial institutions fell from EUR 7,550,960k in FY2022 to EUR 147,811k in FY2023 for the same reason.

Adyen's own headline measure, 'net revenue' (Revenue less costs incurred from financial institutions and costs of goods sold; a line in the statement from the FY2017 statements onwards), in EUR thousands, is: FY2014 46,776 (not published - the FY2015 statements show only Revenues 153,675, costs incurred 106,552 and inventory change 347), FY2015 98,450, FY2016 157,985, FY2017 218,278, FY2018 348,913, FY2019 496,681, FY2020 684,200, FY2021 1,001,517, FY2022 1,330,166, FY2023 1,626,061, FY2024 1,996,074, FY2025 2,364,191. A revenue-growth chart built on this file's revenue field must either be split at FY2023 or use these net revenue figures; the growth story (18-46% a year) is only visible in net revenue.

operatingIncome is 'Income before net finance income and income taxes' (labelled 'Income before interest income, interest expense and income taxes' up to FY2019): after all operating expenses, before finance income/expense and other financial results. FY2016 includes a one-off EUR 56,282k 'Other gains and losses' (the Visa Europe share disposal), which is why FY2016 operating income (119,275k) is higher than FY2017 (93,465k) on flat growth.

netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to the owners of Adyen N.V.; the group has no non-controlling interests in any year, so both equal the statement totals ('Net income attributable to owners of Adyen N.V.', 'Total equity attributable to owners of Adyen N.V.').

totalDebt is the sum of the current and non-current IFRS 16 lease liabilities, the only interest-bearing debt Adyen has ever carried (no bank borrowings, no bonds, in any year). Leases first appear in FY2019, so totalDebt is 0 for FY2014-FY2018. Components in EUR thousands, non-current + current: 2019 50,903+10,791; 2020 118,051+13,434; 2021 119,968+22,996; 2022 169,873+33,200; 2023 172,397+50,666; 2024 173,321+54,935; 2025 183,269+69,097. This matches the Yahoo totalDebt in the snapshot (2022: EUR 203.1m vs USD 216.5m).

capex is 'Purchases of plant and equipment' from the cash flow statement, stored negative. Adyen reports capitalised software on a separate line ('Capitalization of intangible assets') and it is excluded here because the company does not report the two together: 2014 1,425; 2015 1,626; 2016 1,989; 2017 1,344; 2018 2,769; 2019 4,773; 2020 4,795; 2021 2,959; 2022 3,523; 2023 4,138; 2024 3,029; 2025 2,132 (EUR thousands). Yahoo's capex includes them, which accounts for the whole difference between the two capex series.

dividendPerShare is 0 (recorded, not null) in every year: Adyen has never paid a dividend. AR2025 note 37 and AR2023 note 35 state 'No dividend has been paid in the years presented', and the IPO prospectus says the board 'does not anticipate paying dividends'; net income is added to retained earnings.

employees is the number of FTEs at 31 December from note 4 ('FTE per office'), excluding contractors. It is FTE, not headcount: AR2025 puts headcount at 4,780 against 4,771 FTE and AR2024 at 4,354 against 4,345. Older reports' 'average FTE during the year' figures (e.g. 4,271 average in FY2024) are a different measure and were not used.

sharesOutstanding is the number of ordinary shares issued at 31 December, from the share capital note ('resulting in a total of N ordinary shares', nominal value EUR 0.01). There are no treasury shares. The count rises only through option exercises and share plans.

Restatements, latest figure used with restated: true: FY2015 operatingCashFlow was published as 137,903k in the FY2015 statements and restated to 138,398k in the FY2016 statements; FY2016 operatingCashFlow was published as 193,645k in the FY2016 statements and restated to 189,565k in the FY2017 statements (and 189.6 in the prospectus' selected-information table). No other restatement was found: the FY2023 figures in AR2024 are identical to AR2023, and the FY2017/FY2018 figures in AR2019 match AR2018.

Yahoo cross-check (snapshot-2026-10-26.json, USD, divided by the implied average EUR/USD rate): revenue 2022 USD 9,397,790,523 at 1.0517 = EUR 8,935.6m vs 8,935.6m here; 2023 USD 2,021,420,968 at 1.0848 = 1,863.4m vs 1,863.4m; 2024 USD 2,404,223,179 at 1.0803 = 2,225.6m vs 2,225.6m; 2025 USD 2,997,023,597 at 1.1323 = 2,646.9m vs 2,646.9m. netIncome: 2022 593,318,146/1.0517 = 564.1m vs 564.1m; 2023 757,539,008/1.0848 = 698.3m vs 698.3m; 2024 999,414,688/1.0803 = 925.1m vs 925.2m; 2025 1,203,074,957/1.1323 = 1,062.5m vs 1,062.5m. All four years agree within 0.05% using the same rates for revenue and net income, so there is no wrong-line, unit or scope difference - Yahoo's revenue is this same IFRS top line (its 'grossProfit' is Adyen's net revenue). The only trap is the FY2022/FY2023 break described above, which Yahoo's own series shows too (EUR 8.9bn then 1.9bn).

Document trail: the FY2014-FY2017 rows come from the audited consolidated statements in the June 2018 IPO prospectus (367 pp): FY2017 statements at F-18/F-19/F-21, FY2016 statements at F-68/F-69/F-71, FY2015 statements at F-113/F-114/F-116, with FTE at year end on printed p. 158 and the historic share capital table on p. 163. Those pages use embedded subset fonts that pdftotext returns as cipher text; the statements were decoded character by character against known plaintext to read the figures to the thousand.

The FY2018 annual report PDF served from the IR asset link is truncated (73 pages, ending inside the auditor's report), so FY2018 is taken from the AR2019 comparative columns, which cover every field used. The only value read from AR2018 is FY2017 diluted EPS (2.33) from its income statement on p. 65, because the prospectus' audited statements do not present EPS at all.

companies.name: Airbus SE (European Aeronautic Defence and Space Company, EADS N.V., until 2014)
notes: IFRS (EU-endorsed) for all 19 years; no change of accounting framework. The issuer is EADS N.V. for 2007-2013, Airbus Group N.V./SE for 2014-2016 and Airbus SE from the 2017 Dutch conversion; the 2013-2014 documents are filed under both names.

operatingIncome = the IFRS income-statement line "Profit (loss) before financial result and income taxes" (EADS/Airbus call this EBIT). It is the reported figure and contains one-offs: FY2019 includes the EUR 3.6bn bribery settlement inside administrative expenses, FY2020 the COVID charges. Airbus's headline "EBIT Adjusted" is a non-IFRS measure and is higher (FY2025: EUR 7,128m vs EUR 6,082m reported).
totalEquity = equity attributable to owners of the parent (non-controlling interests excluded). totalAssets as per the statement of financial position.

totalDebt = non-current + current "financing liabilities" (bonds, bank borrowings, finance-lease and, from 2019, IFRS 16 lease liabilities). IFRS 16 was adopted on 1 January 2019 without restating 2018 comparatives, so 2007-2018 debt excludes lease liabilities while 2019-2025 includes them (EUR 2,380m of lease liabilities at 31 December 2025 of the EUR 14,249m total).
cashAndEquivalents = the balance-sheet line "Cash and cash equivalents" only; Airbus also holds current and non-current "securities", which are not included (about EUR 13bn at end-2025).

capex = "Purchases of intangible assets, property, plant and equipment, investment property" (Airbus reports the three together), stored negative. It is not the same basis as Airbus's free-cash-flow measure, which also nets customer financing and other items.

dividendPerShare = dividend declared/proposed for the fiscal year (paid the following spring), including special dividends. FY2009 and FY2020 are nil (no distribution); the EUR 1.80 proposed for FY2019 was withdrawn in March 2020 because of COVID-19, so FY2019 is nil; FY2023 = EUR 1.80 + EUR 1.00 special and FY2024 = EUR 2.00 + EUR 1.00 special; FY2025 = EUR 3.20 proposed to the AGM of 15 April 2026 (not yet paid).
sharesOutstanding = shares outstanding at 31 December (issued less treasury shares) from the Total Equity note; it is not the weighted average used for EPS.

IFRS 15 (adopted 1 January 2018, full retrospective) restated FY2017: originally revenue EUR 66,767m, EBIT EUR 3,421m, net income EUR 2,873m, diluted EPS EUR 3.70; the FY2017 row is the restated version from the 2018 Financial Statements. The same transition cut equity attributable at 31 December 2016 from EUR 3,657m to EUR 1,561m and total assets from EUR 111,133m to EUR 107,667m; no document republished the FY2016 income statement on an IFRS 15 basis, so the FY2016 row combines the pre-IFRS 15 P&L with the restated (opening 2017) balance sheet - see the source entries for both figures.

IAS 19 revised (applied 2013) restated 2011 and 2012: FY2011 revenue unchanged but EBIT EUR 1,613m -> EUR 1,541m, net income EUR 1,033m -> EUR 980m, diluted EPS EUR 1.27 -> EUR 1.20; FY2012 EBIT EUR 2,089m and net income EUR 1,197m are the restated figures. The FY2011 balance sheet is the one published in the 2011 Financial Statements (pre-restatement) because no later document republished it.

IFRS 10/IFRS 11 (applied 2014) restated FY2013: revenue EUR 59,256m -> EUR 57,567m, EBIT EUR 2,607m -> EUR 2,570m, net income EUR 1,465m -> EUR 1,473m, diluted EPS EUR 1.84 -> EUR 1.85 (Registration Document 2014, PDF p. 69). The FY2013 balance sheet, cash flow and share count are from the 2013 Financial Statements, i.e. on the pre-IFRS 11 basis.

The 2016 Financial Statements reclassified certain securities and trade liabilities and restated FY2015: cash and cash equivalents EUR 7,489m -> EUR 6,590m, total assets EUR 106,681m -> EUR 105,782m, operating cash flow EUR 3,600m -> EUR 2,891m. FY2014 keeps the figures published in 2015 (a later EUR 190m cash reclassification is disclosed but no restated FY2014 statements were issued).

The 2011 Financial Statements changed the presentation of pension contributions inside operating cash flow, restating FY2009 operating cash flow from EUR 2,438m to EUR 2,265m and FY2010 from EUR 4,996m to EUR 4,443m; the latest figures are used.
Revenue is the income-statement line "Revenue(s)" for an industrial group (no bank/insurer top line involved). Airbus reports in euros, unchanged over the period.
employees = consolidated headcount at 31 December from the "Number of Employees" note (EADS/Airbus report year-end, not average, headcount).

Cross-check against the Yahoo snapshot (docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json, USD): the implied EUR/USD rates back out at 1.0517 (2022), 1.0848 (2023), 1.0803 (2024) and 1.1323 (2025) and reproduce revenue and net income for 2022-2025 to within 0.3%, confirming the line, unit and scope choices. Yahoo totalDebt and cash use wider definitions (leases/ securities) and are not comparable.

companies.name: Bayerische Motoren Werke Aktiengesellschaft
notes: All years are IFRS; the BMW Group has prepared IFRS consolidated statements for the whole 2007-2025 window, so there is no standard change to flag.
revenue is total Group revenue, i.e. including the Financial Services segment (not automotive-only).
operatingIncome is 'Profit before financial result (EBIT)' (called 'Earnings before financial result' up to 2016).

netIncome is profit attributable to shareholders of BMW AG, not total net profit for the year. The difference is the non-controlling interests: FY2025 total net profit EUR 7,451m vs EUR 7,294m attributable; FY2020 EUR 3,857m vs EUR 3,775m.
totalEquity is equity attributable to shareholders of BMW AG (FY2025 total equity incl. non-controlling interests EUR 97,906m vs EUR 95,697m attributable).

totalDebt is the sum of the balance-sheet lines 'Financial liabilities' (non-current) and 'Financial liabilities' (current). BMW itself discloses this total in its financial-position analysis (e.g. FY2025: EUR 110,469m, 41.5% of total assets). It therefore includes lease liabilities and Financial Services refinancing, so it is much larger than a pure bond/bank-loan figure.

operatingCashFlow is the Group 'cash inflow from operating activities' from the consolidated cash flow statement. BMW also publishes an Automotive-segment figure (e.g. FY2015 EUR 11,836m and FY2007-EUR 6,246m); that segment number is NOT used here, which is why the early years look large relative to later ones (the Group figure is dominated by the Financial Services segment's leased-product and sales-financing flows).

capex is BMW's own 'capital expenditure (excluding capitalised development costs)' = investments in property, plant and equipment and other intangible assets, excluding capitalised development costs, shown negative. Capitalised development costs are reported separately by BMW (FY2025: total investment in intangible assets and PP&E per the cash flow statement EUR 10,963m, of which EUR 3,726m capitalised development costs; the capex figure used here is EUR 7,237m). The same definition is used for every year so the series is comparable. Cash-flow-statement capex on the 'total investment in intangible assets and property, plant and equipment' line is EUR 10,963m (2025) and EUR 12,205m (2024).

sharesOutstanding = ordinary shares plus preferred shares in circulation at 31 December (issued less treasury shares). For 2007-2010 the reports give the number of shares in thousands (601,995k ordinary plus 52,196k/52,665k/53,163k preferred); from 2011 the statement of changes in equity gives exact figures. From 2022 the count falls sharply because of the share buyback programme (601,995,196 ordinary -> 554,226,093 at 31.12.2025).

dilutedEPS is the basic/diluted earnings per ordinary share. BMW states that diluted earnings per share equal basic earnings per share in every year of the window. Preferred-share EPS is about EUR 0.02 higher.
dividendPerShare is the dividend per ordinary share for the fiscal year (proposal of the Board of Management for the latest year). The preferred share receives EUR 0.02 more.

Restatements applied: 2013 was restated in the Annual Report 2014 under IAS 8 (net profit 5,314 -> 5,303; operating cash flow 3,614 -> 4,127; EPS 8.10 -> 8.08; equity 35,455 -> 35,412). Equity for 2012 was restated from EUR 30,295m to 30,499m in the Annual Report 2013. 2017 was restated in the Annual Report 2018 (EPS 13.12 -> 13.07, attributable profit 8,620 -> 8,589, equity 54,112 -> 53,772). 2018 was adjusted for the first-time adoption of IFRS 16 in the Annual Report 2019 (attributable profit 7,117 -> 6,974; EPS 10.82 -> 10.60; equity 57,559 -> 57,268). 2021 operating cash flow was restated from 15,903 to 15,914 in the 2022 report. 2024 employees were restated from 159,104 to 157,457 after non-consolidated companies were excluded from 2025 onwards. BMW also restates prior years for presentation changes of 'minor importance' (footnote 1 of the 2025 ten-year comparison).

Employee counts are not fully comparable across the window: up to 2019 temporary staff, interns and apprentices were included (the 2019 figure was adjusted to 133,778 to remove them), and from 2025 non-consolidated companies are excluded.

Cross-check against the Yahoo figures in docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (converted at the snapshot FX rate of 1.1199 USD/EUR, which is only a rough conversion for older years): FY2025 revenue EUR 134.9bn vs 133.5bn here (+1.1%), net income 7.37bn vs 7.29bn (+1.1%), EBIT 10.09bn vs 10.19bn (-0.9%); FY2024 137.3bn vs 142.4bn (-3.5%, explained by the EUR/USD move between the 2024 average and today's rate); FY2023 net income 10.94bn vs 11.29bn and FY2022 16.85bn vs 17.94bn, likewise FX. No scope or line-item differences found. Two deliberate definition differences remain: Yahoo's totalAssets for FY2025 is about EUR 279bn against BMW's balance-sheet total of EUR 266bn, and Yahoo's totalDebt is about EUR 93bn against the EUR 110bn balance-sheet financial liabilities used here; both come from Yahoo's own derivation, not from BMW's statements.

companies.name: Compagnie Financière Richemont SA
notes: IFRS throughout; reporting currency EUR throughout; fiscal year ends 31 March (fiscalYear = calendar year of the March year-end, FY2008..FY2026).

dividendPerShare is the ordinary dividend per A share and is declared in CHF from FY2009 (EUR 0.78 for FY2008). Special dividends of CHF 1.00 were also paid for FY2022, FY2023 and FY2026 (EUR 0.60 special for FY2007) and are not included.

dilutedEPS is EUR per A share / 10 B shares (per unit before the 2008 restructuring), from total profit incl. discontinued operations. FY2008 net income and EPS include the BAT/Reinet stake reported as discontinued operations.

revenue and operatingIncome use the latest re-presented five-year record: FY2022 excludes YNAP (discontinued, as re-presented in the 2024/2026 reports); FY2018 includes royalty income (re-presented in 2021 report); FY2008 re-presented in the 2011 five-year record. Net income is profit attributable to owners of the parent including discontinued operations (e.g. FY2023 EUR 313m after the YNAP write-down).

totalDebt = non-current + current borrowings + bank overdrafts (lease liabilities excluded). cashAndEquivalents = cash at bank and on hand (balance sheet); money-market funds held at FVTPL (EUR 8.7bn FY2026) are excluded.

sharesOutstanding = number of A shares in issue (522,000,000; 537,582,089 from FY2024 after the 2023 warrant exercise). An equal number of B shares exists, each with 1/10 of the economic rights of an A share.
employees = average number of employees (Switzerland + rest of world); FY2022-FY2025 are continuing operations only (YNAP employees excluded: 4,569 / 4,254 / 3,874 / 3,231).
FY2009 annual report not on the IR site; FY2009 taken from comparatives in the 2010 and 2011 reports.

Yahoo check (FY2023-FY2026): the snapshot is in USD at mixed rates; for each year the ratio of our EUR figure to the snapshot value is the same for revenue and net income (1.04 FY2026, 1.13 FY2025, 1.12 FY2024, ~1.16 FY2023), so lines and scope match and the gap is currency conversion only.

companies.name: Deutsche Telekom AG
notes: Accounting: IFRS in every year FY2007-FY2025, EUR, fiscal year ends 31 December. All amounts are in full euro units; the statements report in millions and were scaled by 1,000,000.

totalEquity = "Issued capital and reserves attributable to owners of the parent" from the consolidated statement of changes in equity. Deutsche Telekom's balance-sheet line "Shareholders' equity" includes non-controlling interests and is much larger (FY2025: 92,231m total vs 62,171m attributable, NCI 30,061m); it is not used here.

totalDebt = current + non-current "Financial liabilities" from the consolidated statement of financial position, plus separately presented "Lease liabilities" where they exist. IFRS 16 was first applied on 1 January 2019 and the FY2018 comparatives were not restated, so FY2007-FY2018 are financial liabilities only (finance leases were included there) and the step from FY2018 62,275m to FY2019 86,184m is mostly the on-balance-sheet lease liability (19,835m), not new borrowing. FY2019 86,184m equals the "financial liabilities and lease liabilities" subtotal in DT's net-debt reconciliation; FY2025 146,723m is the sum of the balance-sheet lines (DT's management reconciliation prints 146,722m because of rounding).

capex = "cash outflows for investments in property, plant and equipment" from the consolidated statement of cash flows, stored negative. Intangible assets and spectrum payments are excluded, so capex is well below DT's own "cash capex" KPI (FY2025: cash capex -19.3bn, of which PP&E -12.3bn). Capex was not restated for IAS 19 but was restated for the FY2011/FY2012 property, plant and equipment reclassification in the FY2013 report.

operatingIncome = "profit (loss) from operations (EBIT)" of the consolidated income statement. DT's management-report "at a glance" EBIT is a management-approach figure that keeps the GD Towers tower business in the results of operations up to its sale on 1 February 2023; it is higher than the IFRS EBIT in FY2021 (13.1bn vs 12,580m), FY2022 (16.2bn vs 15,414m) and FY2023 (33.8bn vs 20,798m, which excludes the 13,696m after-tax profit of the discontinued operation). The IFRS income-statement figures are used here for all years.

netIncome = profit attributable to owners of the parent, including discontinued operations: FY2023 17,788m includes 13,696m from GD Towers; FY2012 -5,353m is the year of the large impairment at T-Mobile US.

FY2021 was restated by the FY2023 report after GD Towers was classified as a discontinued operation: net revenue 107,610m (originally 108,794m) and EBIT 12,580m (originally 13,057m); attributable net profit 4,176m is unchanged. FY2021 is therefore not comparable with FY2020 (100,999m), which still contains GD Towers. FY2021 balance-sheet, cash-flow, dividend and employee data are from the FY2021 report, which the FY2023 report did not restate.
FY2022 figures are the comparatives shown in the FY2023 report; the FY2022 report itself was not opened, so it is unverified whether the FY2022 report showed exactly the same amounts.

FY2011 and FY2012 were restated in the FY2013 report for IAS 19 (revised), applied retrospectively: FY2011 revenue 58,653m, EBIT 5,563m (previously 5,586m), attributable profit 538m (previously 557m), total assets 122,496m (previously 122,542m), PP&E purchases -6,090m (previously -6,569m); FY2012 revenue 58,169m, EBIT -3,962m, attributable profit -5,353m, total assets 107,942m.
FY2007 and FY2008 are the restated comparatives of the FY2009 Form 20-F (IAS 1 revised presentation and derivative presentation changes); the FY2007/FY2008 annual reports themselves were not opened.

dividendPerShare is the dividend declared for the financial year (paid the following year). FY2025 EUR 1.00 is the proposed dividend subject to the 2026 shareholders' meeting; FY2013 EUR 0.50 was the first dividend after the 2012 loss.

sharesOutstanding = number of ordinary shares at the reporting date including treasury shares, from the statement of changes in equity (thousands of shares): 4,361,320k in FY2007-FY2009, 4,321,319k in FY2010-FY2012, 4,451,175k FY2013, 4,535,571k FY2014, 4,606,652k FY2015, 4,676,902k FY2016, 4,761,459k FY2017-FY2020, 4,986,459k FY2021-FY2024 and 4,905,190k FY2025 (capital decrease of 81,269k shares in 2025; 2021 capital increase from the T-Mobile US share issuance).

employees = average number of employees in full-time equivalents excluding trainees, as published in the at-a-glance / selected-financial-data tables (rounded by DT to thousands). The jump in FY2009 (258k) is the first-time consolidation of OTE; FY2020 (224k) and the revenue jump reflect Sprint being consolidated from 1 April 2020.

Scope changes affecting comparability: T-Mobile US merger with MetroPCS (2013), OTE and Telekom Srbija (2009), Sprint consolidation (2020), GD Towers sold 1 February 2023, and the principal/agent revenue-recognition change in Q3 2022 that reduced revenue in the years up to and including 2020.

Cross-check against the Yahoo figures in docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (USD divided by fxToUsd 1.1199462): FY2025 revenue 119,646m vs 119,081m (+0.5%) and net income 9,715m vs 9,609m (+1.1%). FY2022-FY2024 differ by 3-7%, but that is an FX artefact rather than a different line or scope: the snapshot converts each year's euro figure at that year's average rate into USD and then divides by the 26 Oct 2026 spot rate. Converting at the year-average rate instead (FY2022 EUR 114,197m x about 1.053 = USD 120.3bn, / 1.1199 = EUR 107.4bn) reproduces Yahoo's 106,687m within about 0.6%; the same holds for FY2023 (108.1bn vs 107,815m) and FY2024 (111.9bn vs 111,032m).

companies.name: Heineken N.V.
notes: IFRS in every year FY2007-FY2025 (Heineken moved to IFRS in 2005), so no standard change inside the period.

revenue is net revenue, i.e. after excise tax expense. From FY2016 Heineken also presents gross revenue (FY2025: net 28,753m vs gross 34,257m); the net figure is the one used here and the one data vendors report.

operatingIncome is "Results from operating activities" (FY2007-FY2016 statements) / "Operating profit" (FY2017-FY2025). Heineken also reports "operating profit (beia)", a non-IFRS measure (FY2025: 4,385m); that is deliberately not used.

totalDebt = non-current borrowings + current borrowings. For FY2007-FY2016 "Bank overdrafts and commercial papers" was a separate line inside current liabilities and is included here; from FY2016 the balance sheet presents cash gross and the overdrafts sit inside current borrowings.

cashAndEquivalents is the balance-sheet "Cash and cash equivalents" line. From FY2016 it is gross of bank overdrafts; the cash-flow statement closing cash is net of them and is lower (e.g. FY2015: 3,232m vs 282m). The gross-up (IAS 7 amendment) also restated FY2015 total assets from 37,714m to 40,122m.
capex = purchase of property, plant and equipment + purchase of intangible assets, stored negative.

Each year is read from the annual report that contains it as the most recent published figure: FY2025 and FY2024 from the 2025 report, and each earlier year from the following year report comparative column where that report restated it (see restated flags), otherwise from its own report -- FY2007 from the 2008 report.

restated=true: FY2007 (accounting policy change, AR2008 note 3(b)); FY2008 (finalisation of the Scottish & Newcastle purchase-price allocation, AR2009, total assets 20,563 -> 20,587); FY2010 (IAS 19 employee benefits, AR2011: operating profit 2,283 -> 2,298, net profit 1,436 -> 1,447, total assets 26,549 -> 26,662, equity 10,228 -> 9,932); FY2012 (revised IAS 19, AR2013: operating profit 3,691 -> 3,697, net profit 2,949 -> 2,914, equity 11,691 -> 11,734); FY2015 (cash gross-up, AR2016); FY2017 (IFRS 15, AR2018: revenue 21,888 -> 21,609 and debt re-presented, 15,513 -> 15,378); FY2018 (IAS 37, AR2019: net revenue 22,471 -> 22,489, operating profit 3,137 -> 3,121, net profit 1,903 -> 1,913, total assets 41,956 -> 42,151, equity 14,358 -> 14,525).

source.page points to the consolidated primary statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow) of the cited report. dividendPerShare comes from the five-year summary of the same report (AR2025 PDF p. 276; AR2016 PDF p. 166 for the 2012-2016 series) and sharesOutstanding from the share-capital / own-shares disclosure of the same report (AR2025 PDF p. 272; AR2016 PDF p. 161).

FY2008 is read from the KU Leuven library copy of the official Heineken N.V. Annual Report 2008; the company-hosted PDF for that year could not be retrieved. The document is the company published report, only the host differs.

employees = average number of employees, FTE (as published). The pre-2012 reports give headcount instead (AR2011 quotes 64,252 for 2011); FY2011 here uses the FTE basis restated in the 2012 report (71,745) so the series is consistent from FY2011 on.

sharesOutstanding = shares outstanding at 31 December excluding own shares (FY2025: 560,557,296 shares of EUR 1.60 nominal). The count steps from 489,974,594 to 576,002,613 in 2010 because of the rights issue that part-funded the FEMSA beer acquisition.
dividendPerShare = total dividend proposed for the fiscal year (interim + final) in EUR per share; FY2020 was cut to 0.70 because the interim dividend was suspended.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (Yahoo, USD): at the implied rates (FY2025 1.1323, FY2024 1.0802, FY2023 1.0848, FY2022 1.0517) revenue and net income agree exactly and totalAssets, totalEquity, cash, totalDebt, dilutedEPS, operatingCashFlow and capex agree to the euro-equivalent, confirming all line definitions. Yahoo operatingIncome sits 1-4% below Heineken operating profit (FY2023 3,097 vs 3,229; FY2025 3,332 vs 3,406), a difference of EBIT definition on Yahoo side, not a different Heineken line.

companies.name: H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB
notes: H&M reports under IFRS in every year covered (IFRS adopted from FY2005); the fiscal year runs 1 December - 30 November, and fiscalYear is the calendar year in which it ends.

revenue is net sales excluding VAT as reported in the group income statement; operatingIncome is the reported operating profit; netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to the shareholders of H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB.

totalDebt = interest-bearing liabilities (liabilities to credit institutions plus other interest-bearing liabilities, i.e. commercial papers/bonds) plus lease liabilities from FY2020; pension provisions excluded. H&M reported no interest-bearing borrowings at all in FY2007-FY2015 (only pension provisions were interest-bearing). Cross-check: FY2024 totalDebt 76,954 less cash 17,340 plus pension provisions 471 equals the company's own stated 'net debt including provisions for pensions and lease liabilities' of 60,085 (51,951 in FY2023).

capex = investments in leasehold and similar rights, other intangible assets, buildings and land and equipment as reported in the group cash flow statement, stored negative. H&M reports no separate 'purchases of PP&E' line.

IFRS 16 was applied from 1 December 2019 (FY2020) using the simplified approach, so FY2019 and earlier balance sheets and cash flows are not restated and are not comparable with FY2020 onward (no lease liabilities or right-of-use assets before FY2020).

FY2007-FY2009 EPS and share counts are the split-adjusted figures published in the 2011 annual report five-year summary (2-for-1 share split in June 2010); they are therefore marked restated. The 2011 report shows 1,655,072 thousand shares and EPS of 8.21 / 9.24 / 9.90 for 2007 / 2008 / 2009, versus 16.42 / 18.48 / 19.80 on the pre-split 827,536 thousand shares originally published.
FY2013 is restated in the 2014 report for IAS 19 Revised: profit after tax SEK 17,093 m versus 17,152 m as originally published (no balance sheet effect).

FY2023 is restated in the 2024 report for the IAS 12 amendment on deferred tax related to right-of-use assets and lease liabilities: profit attributable SEK 8,745 m versus 8,752 m published in the 2023 report, with total assets/equity and deferred tax liabilities also adjusted (SEK 91 m).

dividendPerShare is the ordinary dividend proposed by the board for that fiscal year. No dividend was paid out of FY2019 or FY2020 earnings: the SEK 9.75 proposed for FY2019 was withdrawn in March 2020 and the board proposed SEK 0.00 for both years. FY2025 shows the SEK 7.10 per share proposed to the 2026 AGM (paid in two instalments); FY2024 shows SEK 6.80 proposed to the 2025 AGM.

FY2021 cash flow from operating activities (SEK 44,619 m) is as reported and is inflated by a large positive working-capital change (operating liabilities +12,459 m); the FY2020 figure is the pandemic year.

Share counts are shares outstanding at the closing day: 1,655,072 thousand for FY2007-FY2021 (no treasury shares) and, after the buyback programmes, 1,629,687 / 1,622,548 / 1,604,491 / 1,602,438 thousand for FY2022-FY2025, taken from H&M's five-year summary page on hmgroup.com (https://hmgroup.com/investors/five-year-summary/) and confirmed in the annual reports (e.g. 1,602,438,375 shares at 30 Nov 2025).
employees is the average number of employees for the financial year as published in the five-year summary.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (Yahoo, USD): dividing by the implied per-period rates gives revenue and net income for FY2022-FY2025 that match the official figures to within 0.1% (e.g. FY2025 net income 1,229.6 m USD x 9.888 = SEK 12,158 m), so line, unit and scope agree.

companies.name: Infineon Technologies AG
notes: Accounting standard: all figures are IFRS as issued by the IASB. Infineon's primary accounting standard was US GAAP up to FY2008 and IFRS from 1 October 2008 (stated in the FY2009 Form 20-F); the FY2007 and FY2008 figures here are the IFRS figures presented retrospectively in that filing, not the originally published US GAAP numbers.

FY2007–FY2009 are restated to exclude the DRAM business Qimonda (deconsolidated February 2009) and the Wireline Communications business (sold to Lantiq, closed November 2009). Originally reported FY2007 revenue was EUR 7,679m including Qimonda; the restated continuing-operations figure is EUR 3,660m.

FY2009 is also restated to exclude the Wireless Solutions (baseband) business sold to Intel in Q1 FY2011: revenue was EUR 3,027m in the FY2009 Form 20-F and EUR 2,184m in the later tables (Annual Report 2010 onwards). The later figure is used (restated: true).

Because of that reclassification, FY2008 (which still includes Wireless Solutions) is not directly comparable with FY2009 onwards; no Infineon document found publishes FY2008 excluding Wireless Solutions.

netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to the shareholders of Infineon Technologies AG. For FY2007–FY2009 the group totals included non-controlling interests (FY2009: group net loss EUR 671m per the 20-F, of which EUR 623m attributable; restated group net loss EUR 674m in Annual Report 2011/2012, attributable amount not published there).

operatingIncome is the IFRS "operating profit / operating income" line of the consolidated income statement (it differs from the EBIT-from-continuing-operations figure the company also publishes, e.g. EUR 1,515m vs EUR 1,536m in FY2025).

operatingCashFlow is "net cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations" as printed in the company's tables, so FY2007–FY2011 exclude the discontinued businesses (e.g. FY2011 total operating cash flow was EUR 2,189m including EUR 1,206m from discontinued operations).

capex: from FY2010 the company's line "purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets and other assets" (its free-cash-flow definition); for FY2007–FY2009 intangibles were reported on a separate line, so only purchases of property, plant and equipment (EUR 492m, 308m, 103m) are included. Stored negative.

totalDebt is the company's "Debt" / "Financial debt" line. For FY2007 and FY2008 no single total is published; the figure is the sum of the two published lines (short-term debt and current maturities EUR 336m/207m plus long-term debt EUR 1,227m/963m), which reproduces exactly the EUR 850m "Debt" the company itself reports for FY2009.

cashAndEquivalents is the balance-sheet line "cash and cash equivalents" (end of period). It is much lower than the company's "gross cash position", which also counts current securities (EUR 2,102m at 30 September 2025).

sharesOutstanding: FY2007 and FY2008 are shares issued at 30 September from the consolidated statement of changes in equity; FY2009–FY2012 are "shares outstanding" in the company tables; FY2013 onwards the company reports "shares issued" (treasury shares are not deducted).

dividendPerShare: zero for FY2007–FY2009. FY2009 is shown as "–" in the company tables and no dividend distribution appears in the FY2009 Form 20-F statement of changes in equity for FY2007 or FY2008 either; the first dividend in the company history was the EUR 0.10 proposed for FY2010. The FY2025 figure (EUR 0.35) is the dividend proposed to the 2026 Annual General Meeting.

employees: FY2007 and FY2008 are Infineon employees excluding Qimonda (29,598 and 29,119); the group total including Qimonda was 43,079 and 41,343. FY2009 onwards are group totals on the continuing-operations basis.

companies.name: Kering SA (Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, PPR, until 2013)
notes: All 19 years are IFRS as published by the company; there is no standard change over the period. IFRS 16 was adopted from 2019 and the 2019-2025 figures are on that basis; the primary statements for 2008-2018 were not restated for IFRS 16. Lease liabilities are excluded from totalDebt in every year, so the debt series is comparable across the change.

Convention: each year is taken from the following year's report (comparative column) so it carries the latest restatement published by the company; FY2025 comes from the 2025 Universal Registration Document. restated=true marks the years whose comparative column differs from what the year's own report showed.

totalDebt = non-current borrowings + current borrowings as printed on the balance sheet (house convention). Lease liabilities and other non-current/current financial liabilities are excluded. Sums were not published as a single 'gross debt' line in the earlier Documents de Reference.
operatingIncome = 'Operating income' (resultat operationnel), i.e. after other non-recurring operating income and expenses, not 'recurring operating income'.
netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to owners of the parent (resultat net part du Groupe / equity attributable to the Group).

Large scope breaks from IFRS 5 reclassifications, all visible in the restated columns: Conforama held for sale in 2011 (2010 revenue was first published as EUR 14,605.1m, restated to 11,007.8m); Fnac and Redcats in 2012-13 (2011 revenue was first published as EUR 12,227.2m, restated to 8,062.3m; 2013 revenue first published as 9,748.4m, restated to 9,655.7m; 2012 needed no further restatement, the 2013 and 2012 reports agree at 9,736.3m); PUMA, Stella McCartney, Volcom and Christopher Kane in 2018 (2017 revenue first published as EUR 15,477.7m, restated to 10,815.9m); Kering Beaute in 2025 (2024 revenue first published as EUR 17,194m, restated to 16,874m and operating income from 2,312m to 2,198m).

2007-2009 also carry earlier restatements: 2009 revenue was first published as EUR 16,524.6m and restated to 13,584.3m; 2008 revenue was first published as EUR 20,201.2m and restated to 17,207.0m; 2007 revenue was first published as EUR 19,745.8m and restated to 19,098.2m. 2013 net income of EUR 49.6m is after EUR 822.9m of losses on discontinued operations (Redcats and Fnac). FY2007's balance sheet is the one printed in the 2008 Reference Document (total assets 28,212.1m, group equity 9,218.2m); the 2009 Reference Document's opening column restates those two to 28,156.9m and 9,128.0m when it splits out assets held for sale, a difference of 0.2% and 1.0% that does not affect any P&L line.

employees = headcount on the payroll at year-end as published (note 'Headcount on the payroll at year-end' from 2015, 'registered workforce at December 31' in the PPR-era sustainability chapter). It is not average FTE, which the company also publishes and which is lower (2025: 43,228 average FTE vs 43,731 at December 31). For 2007-2012 the published tables give four manager/non-manager category totals but no grand total, so those six figures are the sum of the four printed category totals in the year-end workforce table (e.g. 2012: 2,638 + 2,780 + 16,813 + 11,208).

The employee series is not comparable across scope breaks: 2008 76,864 and 2009 59,821 include the retail businesses later sold; 2010 42,357 and 2011 28,957 are the restated columns after the Conforama and Redcats disposals; 2017 28,897 is restated for PUMA; 2024-2025 include Kering Beaute, which is otherwise presented as a discontinued operation.

dividendPerShare = net dividend declared for the year, subject to AGM approval in the year it was proposed. FY2019 was proposed at EUR 11.50 and cut to EUR 8.00 in April 2020; the 8.00 actually paid is shown. FY2025 shows the ordinary EUR 3.00 per share only; an exceptional EUR 1.00 per share was also proposed for FY2025 and is not included in the field.

sharesOutstanding is the number of shares outstanding at December 31 as published (par value EUR 4). 2025 = 122,620,351 'issued and outstanding'; 2018-2024 are taken from the statements of changes in equity; 2007-2017 from the share capital / EPS notes of the relevant report.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json using period-average EUR/USD rates: 2025 revenue 14,675m x 1.13 = 16,583m vs 16,616m and net income 72m vs 81.5m USD; 2024 16,874m x 1.082 = 18,258m vs 18,228m and 1,133m vs 1,224m; 2023 19,566m x 1.0824 = 21,178m vs 21,225m and 2,983m vs 3,236m; 2022 20,351m x 1.0535 = 21,440m vs 21,403m and 3,614m vs 3,801m. All within 0.5%, so the lines and units are right (Yahoo's annual figures use each year's average rate, not the snapshot's current fxToUsd of 1.1199; the implied EUR/USD rate is identical for revenue and net income in each of the four years: 1.1323, 1.0803, 1.0848, 1.0517). Yahoo's 2024 revenue matches the restated 16,874, not the 17,194 first published. Yahoo's balance-sheet block does not reconcile (2025 totalAssets and equity are ~3.7% above the filed statements, 2024 ~3.7% below, and its totalDebt includes lease liabilities), so those fields were taken from the company statements only.

Kering's Documents de Reference for 2008-2012 and the 2007-2014 files are no longer served from kering.com; they were read from the Internet Archive copies of the original ppr.com/kering.com PDFs (the URLs in source.url). The 2016-2024 files are the live kering.com documents.

notes: IFRS (EU-endorsed) throughout FY2007-FY2025: LVMH has reported under IFRS since 2005, so there is no local-GAAP year and no standard change inside the window.

operatingIncome = the "Operating profit" line of the consolidated income statement (résultat opérationnel, i.e. after other non-recurring operating income and expenses). LVMH's headline KPI is "Profit from recurring operations" (résultat opérationnel courant), which is higher: 2025 17,755; 2024 19,571; 2023 22,802; 2022 21,055; 2021 17,151; 2020 8,305; 2019 11,504; 2018 10,003; 2017 8,293; 2016 7,026; 2015 6,605; 2014 5,715; 2013 6,017; 2012 5,924; 2011 5,263; 2010 4,321; 2009 3,352; 2008 3,628; 2007 3,555 (EUR millions). Yahoo's operatingIncome is the recurring figure.

capex = "Acquisitions of intangible assets and property, plant and equipment" as published by LVMH in the business review (FY2018-FY2025), stored negative. That published figure is identical to the "net cash used in purchases of fixed assets" line of the operating-investments note (e.g. FY2018: 2,990), so the same line is used for FY2007-FY2017. It is net of the change in fixed-asset payables and of assets acquired under finance leases, hence slightly below gross capital expenditure.

totalDebt = long-term borrowings + short-term borrowings ("gross borrowings") from the consolidated balance sheet; lease liabilities (IFRS 16, from 2019) and purchase commitments for minority interests' shares are excluded.

cashAndEquivalents = "Cash and cash equivalents" on the balance sheet. The cash-flow statement's closing figure is lower because it is net of bank overdrafts (FY2025: 8,359 vs 8,794; FY2018: 4,413 vs 4,610; FY2008: 718 vs 1,013).
netIncome and totalEquity are the amounts attributable to owners of the parent ("Net profit, Group share" / "Equity, Group share").

Restatements (latest published figure used, restated=true): FY2007 balance sheet restated in the FY2008 document for the offsetting of income tax assets and liabilities against advance tax payments; FY2008 restated in the FY2010 document for the IAS 38 amendment (total assets 31,577 -> 31,483; equity 12,897 -> 12,804); FY2011 restated in the FY2013 document for amended IAS 19 (equity 22,451 -> 22,371); FY2012 restated in the FY2014 document for IFRS 11 (total assets 49,930 -> 49,850); FY2013 restated in the FY2014/FY2015 documents for IFRS 11 and the Loro Piana purchase price allocation; FY2016 and FY2017 restated in the FY2018 document for IFRS 9 and the Christian Dior Couture purchase price allocation (FY2017 net profit 5,129 -> 5,365, diluted EPS 10.18 -> 10.64; FY2016 net profit 3,981 -> 4,066).

Budget/scope breaks to keep in mind: FY2018 was explicitly NOT restated for IFRS 16 (footnote in the 2020 URD), so its balance sheet carries no right-of-use assets or lease liabilities, while FY2019 onwards do (FY2020 long-term borrowings jump by 9 billion euros for that reason, and cash rises to 19,963 as debt was pre-funded). FY2014 net profit (5,648) includes 2,677 million euros (5.34 euros per share) from the distribution in kind of the Hermès shares, so it is not comparable with neighbouring years.

Revenue for FY2012 and FY2013 is the reclassified figure published from the FY2014 document onwards (27,970 and 29,016, versus 28,103 and 29,149 as first reported) - a 133 million euro reclassification in both years.

FY2007-FY2017 figures come from LVMH's "Documents financiers / Financial documents" (condensed consolidated statements with three-year comparatives). LVMH no longer serves those PDFs from lvmh.com (the old r.lvmh-static.com links now redirect to the homepage), so the Internet Archive copies of the original files are cited; each cited archive URL was opened and its byte size matches the file read. FY2018-FY2025 come from the Universal Registration Documents hosted on lvmh.com. Each year is taken from the latest document that reports it as a comparative: FY2007 from FY2008, FY2008 from FY2010, FY2009 from FY2011, FY2010 from FY2012, FY2011 from FY2013, FY2012 from FY2014, FY2013-FY2014 from FY2015, FY2015 from FY2017, FY2016-FY2017 from FY2018, FY2018-FY2019 from the 2020 URD, FY2020-FY2021 from the 2022 URD, FY2022 from the 2022 URD, FY2023 from the 2024 URD, FY2024-FY2025 from the 2025 URD.

dividendPerShare = gross dividend per share for the fiscal year as published in the group's "Data per share"/highlights page (FY2007-FY2008: amount paid during the period; FY2025: amount proposed to the AGM). FY2020 2.00 interim + 4.00 final = 6.00; FY2019 2.20 + 2.60 = 4.80; FY2018 2.00 + 4.00 = 6.00 - the FY2019 total is lower only because its final dividend was 2.60 rather than 4.00.

sharesOutstanding = number of shares in issue at 31 December per the statement of changes in equity (treasury shares held remain in issue). The 2011 jump from 490,642,232 to 507,815,624 is the 18,037,011 shares issued for Bulgari plus option exercises; later decreases are share retirements (LVMH cancels the shares it buys back).

employees = total headcount at 31 December (permanent + fixed-term contracts) from the group's "Total workforce as of December 31" table: FY2018 156,088; FY2019 163,309; FY2020 150,479; FY2021 175,647; FY2022 196,006; FY2023 213,268; FY2024 215,637. FY2025 211,552 excludes apprenticeships and vocational training contracts (all-in workforce 213,932), so FY2025 is slightly narrower in scope than FY2023-FY2024. The FY2007-FY2017 Financial Documents publish no headcount at all, hence null.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (USD, divided by the implied average rate): revenue and net income agree to the million for FY2022-FY2025 (implied rates 1.0517 / 1.0849 / 1.0802 / 1.1323), e.g. FY2025 revenue 91,496.0m USD / 1.1323 = 80,807m EUR and net income 12,316.9m USD / 1.1323 = 10,878m EUR; FY2022 83,278.6 / 1.0517 = 79,184 and 14,812.5 / 1.0517 = 14,084. Yahoo's operatingIncome is "Profit from recurring operations", not the "Operating profit" stored here (FY2025 17,755 vs 17,099), and its dilutedEPS for FY2025 is a USD-converted 24.74 (21.85 EUR).

FY2007's balance sheet is as published in the FY2008 document, which restated it only for income-tax offsetting. The IAS 38 amendment adopted in 2010 applied retrospectively to 1 January 2007, but LVMH presented only the restated FY2008 comparative, so an IAS 38-consistent FY2007 balance sheet was never published; treat FY2007 totalAssets/totalEquity as the pre-amendment figures.

companies.name: L'Oréal S.A.
notes: All 19 years are IFRS as adopted in the European Union; L'Oréal moved to IFRS in 2005, so no accounting-standard switch occurs inside the FY2007-FY2025 window.

operatingIncome is L'Oréal's published 'Operating profit' line (after cost of sales, R&D, advertising and promotion and SG&A; before 'other income and expenses'). It reconciles exactly with the snapshot's operatingIncome after FX conversion.

totalDebt is L'Oréal's 'current and non-current debt'. For FY2023-FY2025 the company publishes the total directly (8,692.2 / 8,495.0 / 11,916.0 EUR m). For the other years it is the sum of the balance-sheet lines 'non-current borrowings and debt' + 'current borrowings and debt' (+ 'non-current lease debt' + 'current lease debt' from FY2019, when IFRS 16 took effect). Every one of those sums reproduces the net debt L'Oréal itself publishes to within EUR 0.4m (e.g. FY2007 3,459.8 - 1,086.7 cash = 2,373.1 vs published net debt 2,373).

IFRS 16 (leases) adopted 1 January 2019: lease liabilities of EUR 1,628.0m (non-current) and 407.9m (current) enter totalDebt for the first time in FY2019, which is why totalDebt jumps from EUR 1,241m in FY2018 to EUR 2,887m in FY2019 with no change in borrowing policy.

Scope breaks - IFRS 5 discontinued operations: the 2014 Registration Document restated FY2012 (and FY2013) after the announced disposal of 50% of Galderma; FY2012 net sales moved from the 22,462.7 EUR m originally reported in the 2012 Registration Document to 21,638.4 EUR m. FY2007-FY2011 therefore still include Galderma and other proportionally consolidated businesses that FY2012 onwards exclude.

Scope breaks - The Body Shop: the 2017 and 2018 Registration Documents restate FY2015 and FY2016 for IFRS 5. FY2015 net sales 25,257.4 -> 24,290.2 EUR m and operating profit 4,387.7 -> 4,332.9 EUR m; FY2016 25,837.1 -> 24,916.3 and 4,539.9 -> 4,506.1. The restated figures are used here and flagged restated: true. Note that L'Oréal's own later 'L'Oréal 2015-2021' summary table (2021 URD, PDF p. 45) republishes the un-restated 25,257 / 25,837 instead; that table is internally inconsistent with its own 2017 column (26,023), so the primary-statement figures were preferred.

FY2015 and FY2016 balance sheets still include The Body Shop (L'Oréal's own footnote: '2016 and 2015 balance sheets as reported including The Body Shop'), while their income statements exclude it. totalAssets / totalEquity for those two years are therefore on a slightly wider scope than revenue.

Other restatements: FY2013 and FY2014 balance sheets were restated for IFRIC 21 (FY2014 total assets 32,063.0 -> 32,058.8); FY2016 and FY2017 balance sheets were restated for IFRS 9 in the 2018 Registration Document (FY2016 total assets 35,630.2, cash 1,746.0); FY2007 and FY2008 were restated in the 2009 Annual Report for sample/POS costs, customer loyalty programmes and immediate recognition of actuarial gains and losses.

netIncome is 'attributable to owners of the Company' (group share), totalEquity is 'equity attributable to owners of the Company'. Two years carry large one-off items: FY2007 includes a EUR 642.8m pre-tax capital gain on the Sanofi-Aventis shares sold (net profit 2,656.0m vs 2,039m excluding non-recurring items), and FY2014 includes EUR 2,142.7m of net profit from discontinued operations on the Galderma disposal (net profit 4,910.2m, hence the spike in diluted EPS to 8.39).

dividendPerShare is the dividend declared for that financial year (paid the following year). FY2025's 7.20 EUR was proposed to the AGM of 24 April 2026 and was not yet paid when the 2025 URD was filed. Historical path: 1.38 (2007), 1.44, 1.50, 1.80, 2.00, 2.30, 2.50, 2.70, 3.10, 3.30, 3.55, 3.85 (2018), 3.85, 4.00, 4.80, 6.00, 6.60, 7.00, 7.20 (2025).

sharesOutstanding is common shares outstanding net of treasury shares, from each year's consolidated statement of changes in equity. The 2025 URD's parent-company five-year summary prints 557,672,360 for 31.12.2021, but the consolidated statement of changes in equity in the same document prints 535,412,360; the consolidated figure is used (557,672,360 appears to be a typo, since 2022 in the same table correctly reads 535,186,562).

employees is the consolidated headcount in note 5.1 ('excluding employees of equity-accounted companies'). From FY2012 the count excludes equity-accounted businesses (FY2012 70,394 vs 72,637 as published on a proportionally-consolidated basis in the 2012 Registration Document), and FY2015-FY2016 exclude The Body Shop (9,612 and 9,590 staff), so the series carries small definitional breaks at 2012 and 2015. L'Oréal's CSRD sustainability statement reports a wider 'workforce' figure (97,583 for 2025 against 94,610 here).

capex is 'purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets' from the consolidated cash flow statement, sign-normalised to negative. It includes intangibles because L'Oréal reports the two together.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (Yahoo, USD): using the average EUR/USD rate implied by each year, FY2022-FY2025 revenue, operating income, net income, diluted EPS, operating cash flow and capex all reconcile to within 0.1%. Balance-sheet items reconcile once converted at the year-end rate (e.g. FY2025 total assets 61,821.2m x 1.1745 = USD 72,623m vs snapshot 72,623m). No line or scope mismatch found.

companies.name: Hermès International Société en commandite par actions
notes: IFRS throughout: Hermès prepares its consolidated accounts under IFRS as adopted in the EU for every year from 2007 to 2025 (IFRS adopted from 2005); no other standard is involved, so 'standard' is IFRS for all 19 years.
operatingIncome is 'operating income' (résultat opérationnel), which equals recurring operating income in most years; 2007 (+€9.2m), 2018 (+€52.7m) and 2020 (+€91.1m) include non-recurring items.
netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to owners of the parent (excluding non-controlling interests).

operatingCashFlow is 'net cash from operating activities' / 'cash flows related to operating activities (A)', i.e. after interest and income tax paid. Hermès also publishes an 'operating cash flows' subtotal (French CAFG) before working-capital changes, which is higher (2025: €5,607m vs €5,374m) — that subtotal is NOT used here.

capex = purchases of intangible assets + purchases of property, plant and equipment (Hermès' 'operating investments'), stored negative. The 'investments (excluding financial investments)' line in the older five-year summaries also includes investments in associates, so it is larger than capex (e.g. 2009: €207.3m vs €197.7m; 2012: €370.0m vs €263.0m).

totalDebt = borrowings and financial liabilities (current + non-current) + lease liabilities (current + non-current). IFRS 16 was adopted on 1 January 2019 with full retrospective restatement of 2018, so 2018 and later include lease liabilities while 2007-2017 are borrowings only; the increase in totalDebt in 2018 (€53.6m -> €1,166.0m) is almost entirely IFRS 16, not new borrowing.

FY2007 and FY2008 were restated in later reports for the IAS 38 amendment on samples, advertising and promotional expenditure; the restated figures are used (2007 total assets €2,062.5m and equity €1,459.8m, 2008 total assets €2,325.5m and equity €1,588.5m) and both years are flagged restated.

sharesOutstanding is the number of shares comprising the share capital at 31 December (105,569,412 from 2009 onward), which includes treasury shares (about 0.7%); data providers such as the Yahoo snapshot in docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json show the net-of-treasury count (about 104.8m).

employees is the group headcount from the key-data table ('workforce: number of employees' in 2007-2019, 'headcount' from 2020). From 2021 the figure follows the CSRD definition of own workers (permanent + fixed-term contracts with no length-of-service condition), pro forma for 2021-2023 per footnote 6 of the 2025 URD: the 2024/2025 URDs show 26,494 / 25,185 / 22,879 / 20,296 / 18,137 where the 2022 URD had reported 19,686 (2022) and 17,595 (2021) and the 2020 URD 16,600 (2020). The 2020 figure used here (16,956) is the one shown in the 2024/2025 URDs, which differs from the 16,600 reported in the 2020 URD; that difference is not explained in the documents, so 2020-2023 are flagged restated.

dividendPerShare is the net dividend declared in respect of each fiscal year, not the cash paid during it. 2011 (€7.00), 2014 (€7.95) and 2017 (€9.10) include an extraordinary dividend of €5.00 per share; 2023 (€25.00 = €15.00 ordinary + €10.00 exceptional) and 2024 (€26.00 = €16.00 ordinary + €10.00 exceptional) include an exceptional dividend of €10.00 per share (URD 2024 note 13.4, URD 2025 note 12.4). For FY2019 a dividend of €5.00 was proposed in the 2019 URD but €4.55 was actually paid after the June 2020 AGM; the later figure (URD 2022 five-year table) is used. FY2025 is a proposed ordinary dividend of €18.00 (including the €5.00 interim paid in February 2026), subject to the Ordinary General Meeting of 17 April 2026.

The FY2008 document de référence is no longer served from Hermès' own CDN (the 2007-2010 annual reports there start at 2010); the FY2007/FY2008 statements were read from the company's filed 2008 Document de référence as archived at bnains.org, a copy of the AMF-filed document. FY2007 is taken from the 2008 Reference Document and covers continuing operations only: Sagem Communications and Sagem Mobile Phones were presented as discontinued/disposal groups, so FY2007 revenue (€9,714m) and net income (€39m) exclude them.
FY2008 in the 2009 registration document is restated from the 2008 document's figures (profit from operations €603m then, €617m as restated).
IAS 19 revised adopted in 2013: the 2013 document restated FY2012 (equity €5,834m, operating income €1,187m).

IFRS 11 adopted in 2014: the 2014 document re-presented FY2013 and further restated the FY2012 balance sheet (total assets €22,674m, cash €2,083m). FY2012 balance-sheet values stored here are the 2013 document's, i.e. before that second restatement; the FY2012 income statement and cash flow were not changed by IFRS 11.
IFRIC 21 adopted in 2015: FY2014 restated (equity €6,266m).

IFRS 15 adopted in 2018: FY2017 as originally published in the 2017 document was revenue €16,940m, profit from operations €2,681m, net income €4,790m and equity €10,321m; the values stored are the 2018 document's restated comparatives.
IFRS 16 adopted in 2019 with no restatement of 2018.
operatingCashFlow is the 'TOTAL I' line (net cash provided by operating activities), i.e. after changes in working capital, not Safran's 'cash flow from operations' before working-capital changes.

totalDebt is non-current plus current interest-bearing financial liabilities per the balance-sheet note; it excludes 'borrowings subject to specific conditions' (repayable advances, about €1.0bn in 2025), which is why it sits below third-party total-debt figures.

capex is purchases of property, plant and equipment only, stored negative. Safran reports purchases of intangible assets (about €0.6bn in 2025) on a separate cash-flow line, so this figure is lower than a capex measure that adds intangibles.

operatingIncome is the statutory 'Profit from operations' line. Safran also publishes 'adjusted' figures that exclude the effect of hedge accounting on revenue and profit; those are not used anywhere in this file.
FY2019 dividendPerShare is 0: the €2.38 per share dividend in respect of 2019 was cancelled by the Board in 2020 because of Covid-19, so nothing was paid in respect of that year.
FY2025 dividendPerShare of €3.35 is the dividend proposed by the Board and subject to shareholder approval.

employees is the group headcount at 31 December used in Safran's operational reporting. From 2024 the URD also publishes a wider CSRD scope (103,058 for 2024 and 110,778 for 2025) that differs from the 99,364 and 110,535 stored here.

notes: IFRS throughout FY2007-FY2025 (IFRS as endorsed by the EU, also full IFRS); no change of accounting standard in the period, so a standard switch is not a factor. Fiscal year ends September 30; fiscalYear is the calendar year the fiscal year ends in.
revenue = the revenue line of the consolidated income statement (continuing operations), read from the latest document that republished the year (normally the five-year summary of a later report).

operatingIncome = 'Income from continuing operations before income taxes'. Siemens publishes no consolidated EBIT / operating-profit line (its segments report an 'operating profit', but that is not a group income-statement line).

netIncome = net income attributable to shareholders of Siemens AG; totalEquity = total equity attributable to shareholders of Siemens AG. The five-year summaries print only the totals including non-controlling interests (FY2025: total net income EUR 10,387m, total equity EUR 68,371m), so the attributable figures were read from the consolidated income statement and statement of financial position.

totalDebt = the 'Debt' line of the five-year summaries / 'Total debt' of the 20-F capital structure tables = short-term debt and current maturities of long-term debt plus long-term debt. Taken as published, not summed.
capex = 'Additions to intangible assets and property, plant and equipment' from the cash flow statement (in the older 20-Fs the same line), stored negative.

dilutedEPS is the diluted earnings per share for continuing and discontinued operations (the whole-group line: FY2025 EUR 12.11), matching the whole-group netIncome; Siemens also prints a continuing-operations EPS (FY2025 EUR 9.52) which is not used here.

totalEquity for FY2010-FY2013 is the attributable figure published in the capital-structure tables of the Form 20-F filings (FY2013: EUR 28,111m, confirmed again in the FY2014 annual report); no later document republishes attributable equity for those years, because the later five-year summaries carry only total equity including non-controlling interests. FY2010 and FY2011 attributable equity and cash are from the FY2011 Form 20-F, i.e. before IFRS 11 was applied (IFRS 11 left FY2013 attributable equity unchanged at 28,111).

sharesOutstanding = shares outstanding at September 30 for FY2007-FY2013 (disclosed in Item 3 of the 20-F filings). From FY2014 the annual reports publish no period-end count, so the basic weighted average number of shares outstanding from the earnings-per-share note is used (FY2025: 785,093 thousand). The two definitions differ by less than 1%.
employees = headcount at September 30 on a continuing-operations basis as printed in the five-year summaries; null for FY2007-FY2009 (see gaps).

Restatement chain, latest figure used each time: IFRS 11 (adopted FY2014) removed proportionate consolidation of joint ventures and cut FY2010-FY2013 revenue by about 4% (FY2010 67,862 -> 65,067; FY2011 72,526 -> 69,607; FY2012 77,395 -> 74,734 -> 74,087; FY2013 75,882 -> 73,445 -> 72,782) while total net income was unchanged. IFRS 15 from FY2018 restated FY2017 (revenue 83,049 -> 82,863, total assets 133,804 -> 136,111, diluted EPS 7.29 -> 7.19, net income attributable 6,046 -> 5,961, employees 372 -> 377). IFRS 9 from the Sep 30, 2018 balance sheet; IFRS 17 in the Sep 30, 2023 balance sheet.

Scope breaks to be aware of: Siemens Energy and Siemens Gamesa were classified as discontinued operations in FY2020, Flender in FY2021 and Innomotics in FY2024. From FY2018 the reported revenue, operating cash flow, capex and employees are continuing operations only (FY2018 revenue 83,044 -> 55,538; FY2019 86,849 -> 56,797; FY2022 71,977 -> 69,519; FY2023 77,769 -> 74,882), while netIncome is the whole-group figure attributable to shareholders and therefore still contains the discontinued businesses. FY2017 revenue (82,863) is on the pre-FY2020 basis because Siemens did not restate periods before FY2018.

FY2007-FY2009 come from the Form 20-F filings (Siemens' last 20-F is fiscal 2013). Nothing republished them after IFRS 11, so their revenue is on the older basis (FY2009: 70,053 originally, 68,726 in the 2013 filing), whereas FY2010-FY2011 revenue are the IFRS 11 values from the FY2014 annual report. Net income attributable for FY2007-FY2009 is the figure published before those reclassifications (FY2007 3,806, FY2008 5,725, FY2009 2,292).

20-F source references point to the EDGAR HTML filings: Item/section plus the F-page numbers of the audited statements in Item 18, because no paginated PDF of those filings was used. Where a year needed two documents, the second document's URL is given in the source.document text.

Five-year-summary links: Siemens stores each year's 'Five-Year Summary' PDF under a content hash that changes when the file is re-published, so the three summary links (fiscal 2017, 2018 and 2019 editions) were refreshed from the hashes that the IR annual-reports page (irUrl) currently publishes and the cited columns re-read; every URL in this file was re-opened and returned a PDF/HTML document.

Yahoo cross-check (snapshot-2026-10-26, USD at the fiscal-year average rate): FY2025 revenue 78,914 x 1.1066 = 87,320 vs 87,320; FY2024 75,930 x 1.0872 = 82,550 vs 82,548; FY2025 net income 9,620 x 1.1066 = 10,645 vs 10,645; FY2024 8,301 x 1.0872 = 9,025 vs 9,025; FY2023 and FY2022 net income also match at the average rates (8,509 and 4,020). The only gap above 3% is FY2022 revenue: Yahoo carries USD 77,716, which corresponds to the pre-Innomotics figure of EUR 71,977m, while this file uses the restated EUR 69,519m (about 3.4% lower).

companies.name: Schneider Electric S.E.
notes: IFRS as adopted by the EU for every year from FY2007 to FY2025 (Schneider Electric moved to IFRS in 2005, so no standard change falls inside this window). Reporting currency EUR throughout; fiscal year ends December 31.

** 2-for-1 share split in 2011. Shares in issue went from 271,959,091 at Dec 31, 2010 to 548,943,024 at Dec 31, 2011. dilutedEPS, dividendPerShare and sharesOutstanding for FY2007-FY2010 are the figures the company published at the time (pre-split) and are NOT comparable with FY2011 onwards; no post-split restatement of those years exists in any document found, so none was computed.

Field definitions: revenue = 'Revenue' on the consolidated income statement (the 2008 report labels the same line 'Revenue'); operatingIncome = 'Operating income' ('Operating profit' in the 2008 report) i.e. after amortisation and impairment of purchase-accounting intangibles, before net financial income - it is NOT 'Adjusted EBITA' (which excludes restructuring, other operating income/expenses and PPA amortisation and is higher); netIncome = profit attributable to owners of the parent; totalEquity = equity attributable to owners of the parent; cashAndEquivalents = 'Cash and cash equivalents' on the balance sheet (Schneider's cash-flow statement reports a slightly different 'net cash and cash equivalents'); totalDebt = 'TOTAL CURRENT AND NON-CURRENT FINANCIAL LIABILITIES' (bonds, bank borrowings, commercial paper, accrued interest, bank overdrafts, short-term portion of debt), i.e. gross financial debt, excluding pension provisions and purchase commitments over non-controlling interests, which the company reports separately in its net-debt table; operatingCashFlow = 'TOTAL I - CASH FLOWS FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES' (after the change in working capital), not the 'net cash provided by operating activities' line shown before the working-capital movement; capex = purchases of property, plant and equipment + purchases of intangible assets, stored negative - Schneider reports the two on separate lines and does not net proceeds from disposals; dividendPerShare = net dividend per share in respect of the fiscal year (the proposed dividend where it had not yet been approved when the report was published).

employees = the Group average number of permanent and temporary employees ('TOTAL AVERAGE WORKFORCE' in note 25 of recent URDs, 'TOTAL AVERAGE NUMBER OF EMPLOYEES' in the notes of the 2008-2017 reports), not the year-end head count (e.g. 162,970 average vs 159,844 head count at Dec 31, 2025). From FY2024 the definition excludes non-employee interim workers; FY2024 therefore uses the 158,635 restated in the 2025 URD (the 2024 URD published 176,962 including 18,809 interim workers).
sharesOutstanding = 'Number of shares in issue' at December 31 from the Article L.232-8 five-year table of the parent company (not the weighted average used for EPS).

Restatements applied (each year is taken from the latest document that shows it): FY2009 restated in the 2010 report (net income attributable 852 -> 824; total assets 25,649 -> 25,632; equity attributable 11,757 -> 11,729); FY2011 restated in the 2012 report; FY2012 restated in the 2013 report (net income 1,840 -> 1,813; diluted EPS 3.36 -> 3.31; total assets 36,156 -> 36,150; equity 16,642 -> 16,653); FY2013 restated in the 2014 report for discontinued operations (revenue 23,551 -> 23,392; operating income 3,091 -> 3,039; total assets 36,988 -> 37,349; equity 17,212 -> 17,211; cash 5,528 -> 5,563; total financial liabilities 8,859 -> 8,889; operating cash flow 2,901 -> 2,866; capex -822 -> -814); FY2016 restated in the 2017 report (revenue 24,693 -> 24,459; operating income 2,951 -> 2,975; operating cash flow 2,970 -> 2,957; capex -859 -> -836; average workforce 170,866 -> 160,924).

FY2007 and FY2008 come from the 2008 Registration Document (the earliest one still published by the company), FY2009-FY2010 from the 2010 document, FY2011 from the 2012 document, FY2012 from the 2013 document and FY2013-FY2014 from the 2014 document; from FY2015 each year is taken from its own annual/universal registration document, except FY2016 (from the 2017 report, which restates it) and FY2024 (from the 2025 URD, for the restated workforce).

Dividend anomaly: the five-year table in the 2022 URD prints 2.63 as the FY2022 net dividend per share, which contradicts its own 'dividends paid' row and the 2023, 2024 and 2025 URDs (all 3.15), and the 2023 URD's text states 'In 2023, the Group paid out the 2022 dividend of EUR 3.15 per share'. FY2022 uses 3.15.

Yahoo cross-check (FY2022-FY2025): the snapshot values are in USD. Revenue and net income imply the same EUR/USD rate for each year (1.052 for 2022, 1.085 for 2023, 1.080 for 2024, 1.132 for 2025), so the lines, units and scope match and the whole gap is currency conversion.

gaps: FY2007-FY2025 totalDebt: Volkswagen does not publish a single group total-debt figure; it reports Automotive net liquidity and Financial Services financial liabilities separately
FY2007-FY2025 sharesOutstanding: not taken (two share classes: ordinary and preferred)
notes: IFRS throughout. Each year's figures are taken from the following year's annual report (prior-year column) so that restatements are reflected; FY2025 from Annual Report 2025

revenue = sales revenue; operatingIncome = operating result (FY2007-FY2010 'operating profit'); revenue, operating result, total assets and operating cash flow follow the latest Five-Year Review (AR2025 for 2021-2025, AR2020 for 2016-2020, AR2015 for 2011-2015, AR2010 for 2007-2010)

netIncome = earnings attributable to Volkswagen AG shareholders (excludes hybrid capital investors and noncontrolling interests); totalEquity = equity attributable to Volkswagen AG shareholders (excludes hybrid capital and noncontrolling interests)
dilutedEPS and dividendPerShare are per PREFERRED share (VOW3 is the preferred line); basic and diluted are equal from FY2010; FY2025 dividend is the proposal to the 2026 AGM
operatingCashFlow = Group cash flows from operating activities; FY2007 and FY2008 were adjusted in AR2010 (originally 15,662M and 10,799M) after a change in presentation

capex = Group investments in property, plant and equipment, investment property and intangible assets excluding capitalized development costs (FY2007-FY2012: acquisition of property, plant and equipment); capitalized development costs (e.g. 9,047M in 2025) are excluded
employees = total workforce at Dec. 31 including the Chinese joint ventures (Key Figures); FY2017-FY2023 published in thousands to one decimal
FY2015 loss reflects diesel-issue special items of 16.9bn; FY2017 operating cash flow is negative because of diesel payments

Yahoo net income is 4-9% higher in 2022-2025 because it includes the share attributable to hybrid capital investors; this file follows the brief (owners of the parent excluding hybrid capital), e.g. 2025 earnings after tax 6,904M, of which Volkswagen AG shareholders 6,673M
